text:
{
  "status": "partial",
  "rpwd_relevant_sections": [
    "Section 31: Free education and appropriate environment for children with benchmark disabilities in a neighborhood or special school"
  ],
  "ncte_relevant_sections": [
    "Guideline p. 30: Transacting curriculum through total communication approach, adapting/differentiating curriculum, and providing adequate facility of resource persons such as speech therapists and occupational therapists",
    "Guideline p. 30: Developing assessment tools that are inclusive by design for continuous feedback",
    "Guideline p. 32: Monitoring the nature, frequency, and extent of required support and strengthening it as needed"
  ],
  "identified_gaps": [
    "Gap 1: The IEP lacks provision for specialized therapeutic support services (such as occupational therapy for visual-motor integration and speech/language support) as mandated by NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30).",
    "Gap 2: Explicit formal review mechanisms to monitor the frequency, nature, and extent of support services are missing, violating NCTE/NCERT implementation standards."
  ],
  "mandatory_accommodations": [
    "Provision of multi-sensory structured literacy and assistive text-to-speech/speech-to-text tools with RPwD Act Section 31 appropriate environment mandate",
    "Access to specialized therapeutic services (occupational and speech support) in accordance with NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30)",
    "Inclusive and flexible assessment tools providing continuous feedback per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p. 30)"
  ],
  "compliance_notes": "While the IEP contains excellent multi-sensory strategies, assistive technology, and measurable goals, it is classified as 'partial' because it omits the integration of allied therapeutic services (such as occupational therapy for visual-motor reversals) and formal monitoring mechanisms explicitly required under the NCTE/NCERT Inclusive Education Guidelines."
}
